questions.text: Walk me through how you would approach the most important responsibilities in this role in assistant lawyer.
expectedKeywords: the core skills listed in the job description
questions.evaluationCriteria: Looks for a structured technical approach, sound tradeoffs, and practical delivery steps.

questions.text: What technical decisions would you make to deliver strong results with the core skills listed in the job description?
expectedKeywords: the core skills listed in the job description
questions.evaluationCriteria: Assess depth in architecture, implementation choices, and awareness of tradeoffs.

questions.text: Describe a project where you used the core skills listed in the job description to solve a meaningful business problem. What was your contribution?
expectedKeywords: the core skills listed in the job description
questions.evaluationCriteria: Strong answers include direct ownership, measurable outcomes, and specific execution details.

questions.text: How have you kept your skills current in the required tools and workflows, and how would that help you succeed in this role?
questions.evaluationCriteria: Looks for continuous learning, real application, and role alignment.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to balance speed, quality, and stakeholder expectations while working with cross-functional stakeholders.
questions.evaluationCriteria: Strong answers use a clear situation, actions, results, and communication strategy.

questions.text: Describe a time you received tough feedback on your work. How did you respond, and what changed afterward?
questions.evaluationCriteria: Looks for coachability, ownership, and evidence of improvement.

questions.text: Imagine you join as a assistant lawyer and discover that a key deliverable is slipping because requirements keep changing. What would you do first?
questions.evaluationCriteria: Strong answers show structured triage, stakeholder alignment, and risk management.

questions.text: If you were responsible for the most important responsibilities in this role but had limited time and incomplete information, how would you decide what to tackle first?
questions.evaluationCriteria: Looks for judgment, prioritization framework, and sensible escalation points.
